01.event: Rav Huna, praised Rav Hamnuna as a great man, asked to see him and found he wore no head cloth because he was unmarried.
01.turn: Rav Hamnuna admitted he was unmarried, and Rav Huna was offended.
01.outcome: Rav Huna turned his face away and forbade Rav Hamnuna to see his face until he married.
01.summary: Rav Hisda praised Rav Hamnuna to Rav Huna, who asked to meet him. When Rav Hamnuna came, Rav Huna noticed he did not cover his head as scholars did, and learned the reason was that he was unmarried. Rav Huna turned his face away and told him not to appear before him again until he had married.

02.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi on his deathbed
02.event: As he was dying, Rabbi summoned his sons and then the Sages and gave instructions about his stepmother's honor, his house, his burial servants, his eulogies and his succession.
02.turn: People later learned the meaning of his requests: his attendants died before him, and the crowds came to the cities.
02.outcome: His instructions were carried out and his successors named.
02.summary: As Rabbi lay dying he called his sons and told them to honor their stepmother, to keep his lamp, table and bed ready in their usual places, and said two named servants would serve him in death. He explained he came home every Shabbat eve, and once a neighbor knocked and his maidservant said Rabbi was sitting there, after which he stopped coming. He then called the Sages and asked not to be eulogized in the small towns, for the yeshiva to resume after thirty days, and named his sons Shimon and Gamliel and Hanina bar Hama to their roles.

04.event: A brewer working for someone betrothed a woman with sediment from the beer he was making.
04.turn: The owner found him and said he should use the sharper sediment, and the brewer asked Rava whether this meant the owner had relinquished it.
04.outcome: Rava ruled the owner spoke out of embarrassment and the woman is not betrothed.
04.summary: A brewer making date beer for someone betrothed a woman with sediment from it. The owner found him and said, why not give her from this sharper sediment. The brewer asked Rava whether that showed the owner had given up his rights. Rava said no, that remark applies only to teruma, so she was not betrothed.

05.actor: A man who came before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
05.event: A man claimed another was a Levite because he had read second in the synagogue, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi questioned him.
05.turn: Asked whether it might be mere prominence, the man said a priest read before him.
05.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi accepted his word and raised the man to Levite status.
05.summary: A man came to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and said another man had established himself as a Levite by reading second at the synagogue. The rabbi asked whether that might simply be because he was prominent. The man replied that a priest had read before him. The rabbi then accepted the claim and elevated the man to Levite status.

08.actor: A man who betrothed with a myrtle branch, and Rav Yosef
08.event: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace and Rav Aha bar Huna asked Rav Yosef what to do.
08.turn: Rav Yosef had to rule between Rav's and Shmuel's opinions.
08.outcome: Rav Yosef answered that the man be flogged and the woman be required to receive a divorce document.
08.summary: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace. Rav Aha bar Huna sent the question to Rav Yosef. Rav Yosef replied that the man should be flogged, as Rav held, and that she should still get a bill of divorce, as Shmuel held, in case the branch was worth a peruta somewhere.

09.actor: A woman selling belts and a man who snatched one
09.event: A man snatched a belt from a woman, asked if she would be betrothed to him if he gave it back, and she took it silently.
09.turn: Whether her silence meant consent to betrothal.
09.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled she could say she merely took her own property, so she was not betrothed.
09.summary: A woman was selling belts when a man snatched one. She asked for it back and he said he would give it if she would be betrothed to him. She took it and said nothing. Rav Nahman ruled she could say she only took what was hers, so there was no betrothal.

10.event: Abaye's tenant farmer asked if he could betroth a nursing woman after fifteen months, and Abaye permitted it.
10.turn: Rav Yosef then told Abaye that Rav and Shmuel prohibit it, so Abaye realized he had given the wrong ruling.
10.outcome: Abaye ran after the farmer but could not catch him, and concluded one should not rule in the teacher's presence.
10.summary: Abaye's tenant farmer asked whether he could betroth a nursing woman after fifteen months, and Abaye permitted it with several reasons. When Abaye told Rav Yosef, he was told Rav and Shmuel require twenty-four months. Abaye ran three parasangs after the farmer but did not catch him. He concluded that one should not rule in front of one's teacher since it was bound to go wrong.

11.actor: The sons of the two wives of bar Tzartzur, and Rav Amram
11.event: After the estate of the house of bar Tzartzur appreciated, the heirs came to Rav Amram about collecting the mothers' marriage contracts.
11.turn: The sons refused his request to appease the others and he threatened excommunication, then sent them to Rav Nahman.
11.outcome: Rav Nahman ruled the heirs had acquired their rights as of the father's death.
11.summary: The estate of bar Tzartzur had been small and then grew, and the sons of his two wives came before Rav Amram. He told the sons of the larger marriage contract to appease the others, but they ignored him. He threatened to excommunicate them and sent them to Rav Nahman, who ruled the heirs acquired their rights when the father died.

12.actor: A woman who came to the court of Rabbi Yehuda
12.event: A woman came to Rabbi Yehuda's court to testify of her husband's death and the people there told her to mourn and tear her clothes.
12.turn: The Gemara asks if they told her to lie and explains they feared Rabbi Yehuda's stricter view.
12.outcome: She was told to act as a mourner so that he would also permit her to remarry.
12.summary: A woman came to Rabbi Yehuda's court. Those present told her to lament her husband, tear her clothes and unbind her hair. The Gemara explains they held with the Rabbis that she could remarry anyway, but advised this so that Rabbi Yehuda would permit it too.

13.event: Funerals had become so costly that relatives abandoned the dead, until Rabban Gamliel had himself buried in plain linen.
13.outcome: Everyone followed him, and by Rav Pappa's day even cheap rough cloth was used.
13.summary: Burials had become so burdensome that relatives would leave the dead and flee. Rabban Gamliel humbled himself and arranged to be taken out in plain linen. All the people followed his example, and Rav Pappa said the practice continues even with cheap cloth.

14.actor: A man who came before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
14.event: A man claimed someone was a Levite because he read second at the synagogue, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi questioned him.
14.turn: Asked if it was just prominence, the man said a priest had read before him.
14.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi raised him to Levite status.
14.summary: A man told Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi that someone had shown he was a Levite by reading second in the synagogue. The rabbi asked whether that was just due to prominence. The man said a priest had read first, so the rabbi accepted it and elevated him to Levite status.

15.event: Rav Anan sent a friendly letter asking Rav Huna to give a woman a tenth of her father's estate, and Rav Huna answered sharply through Rav Sheshet.
15.turn: Rav Anan, offended and puzzled by the word marzeiha, consulted Mar Ukva.
15.outcome: Mar Ukva explained that marzeiha means a mourner and that Rav Anan had been presumptuous in addressing Rav Huna so familiarly.
15.summary: Rav Anan wrote to Rav Huna as a friend, asking him to give a woman a tenth of her father's estate. Rav Huna sent Rav Sheshet with a sharp reply on pain of excommunication. Rav Sheshet delivered it reluctantly. Rav Anan, hurt and not knowing the word marzeiha, went to Mar Ukva, who explained it means mourner and said he had no business using such familiar language to Rav Huna.

16.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi as he was dying
16.event: As he was dying Rabbi named Babylonian places and their faults, including a town whose people trapped fish on Shabbat.
16.turn: Rabbi Ahai excommunicated them and they became apostates.
16.outcome: He ended by noting a righteous man was there and that Rav Yehuda was born that day.
16.summary: As Rabbi lay dying he listed places in Babylonia and what was wrong or right with them. In one, people trapped fish from an overflowing ditch on Shabbat, were excommunicated by Rabbi Ahai and left the faith. He ended by saying a righteous man sat in the lap of Abraham that day and that Rav Yehuda was born in Babylonia.
16.missing: Mostly a list of remarks, with only one small event.

17.actor: The people of the Upper Galilee
17.event: They bought a litra of meat every day for a poor person of noble descent from Tzippori.
17.turn: The Gemara asks what was remarkable about it.
17.outcome: The explanations are that it was poultry, costly meat, or a whole animal lost for him daily.
17.summary: People of the Upper Galilee once bought a litra of meat every day for a poor man of good family from Tzippori. The Sages then debate what made this remarkable: poultry, costly meat, or a village slaughtering an animal daily for him.
17.missing: No turn or ending to the incident itself.

18.actor: A man who betrothed a woman within three months of her divorce or widowhood
18.event: A man betrothed such a woman and fled, and the question came before Rafram.
18.turn: Rav Aha and Rafram disagreed on whether to excommunicate him.
18.outcome: Rafram ruled that his flight is sufficient for him.
18.summary: A man betrothed a woman during the three-month waiting period and ran away. Rav Aha and Rafram disagreed about excommunicating him. When it actually happened, Rafram told people his flight was enough.
18.missing: The incident is only a bare mention; the man's and woman's circumstances are not told.

19.actor: Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Akiva and the Elders
19.event: Gathered in a loft in Lod, they were asked whether study or action is greater.
19.turn: Tarfon said action and Akiva said study.
19.outcome: All concluded that study is greater because it leads to action.
19.summary: Rabbi Tarfon and the Elders were reclining in a loft in Lod when asked whether study or action is greater. Tarfon said action, Akiva said study, and everyone then agreed study is greater because it leads to action.
19.missing: It is a recorded debate with a conclusion rather than events.

20.event: A woman was obliged to swear in Rava's court, and his wife said the woman was suspect; separately Rav Pappa tried to testify a document was paid.
20.turn: Rava turned the oath over to the other party on his wife's word, but would not accept Rav Pappa's single testimony.
20.outcome: Rava explained he trusted his wife because he knew her to be truthful, but did not have the same certainty about Rav Pappa.
20.summary: A woman was ordered to take an oath before Rava, but his wife said she was untrustworthy about oaths, so Rava shifted the oath to the other side. Another time Rav Pappa told Rava a document had been paid, but Rava refused to rely on one witness. Rav Adda bar Mattana asked why Pappa was not trusted like Rava's wife, and Rava said he knew his wife was always truthful but lacked such certainty about Pappa.
20.missing: Two separate incidents are combined in the passage.
